# CHAPTER THREE — S6 THE MANY JOBS · S7 THE HANDOVER · S8 THE TABLE

2026-09-03 · Scene direction for stages 6–8 of the film body, authored under
`docs/2026-09-03-world-direction.md` (THE KEPT WORLD — law), `docs/story.md` (locked),
`docs/copy-spec.md` (verbatim), `docs/2026-09-02-experience-design.md` (structure and
timings inherited unchanged), `docs/2026-09-02-motion-system.md` (clocks and lanes).
Line references are current `world.ts` / `timeline.ts` under `story/src/film/`.

This chapter converts. S6 proves breadth without a feature list. S7 must make `pitch1`
and `pitch2` land as conclusions the visitor has already verified. S8 must make a DM
understand what the product IS in one breath, and want it.

## 0. Chapter rulings — resolutions this chapter makes (cheap to veto, read first)

The direction doc mandates seven S6 subject groups (road, monster, sign, saplings,
chest, NPC, candles — its own S6 asset column) against six islets ("one subject each",
§9). The experience doc's See-list (road, sign, tree, chest, NPC, candles) and its
Sell-list ("roads, encounters, signage, treasure, NPCs, lighting") disagree with each
other about the monster. Resolution, this chapter:

- **R1 — The six vignettes are the Sell-list, in the Sell-list's order:** road ·
  monster (encounters) · sign · chest (treasure) · NPC (villages) · candles (lighting).
  This satisfies the direction's monster-repaint ruling AND its NPC-miniature ruling
  AND the register's "NPC as vignette 5" (1-based). The tree-planting job demotes from
  subject to **dressing on the village islet** — the sapling trio (R) stands at the
  village edge with a fresh soil pat-mark and a draughting X where the next tree goes.
  "Dungeon gates opened" stays folded into S3's cave door, as v1 already decided.
- **R2 — `plantAndPat` plays on the NPC's base.** The verb list names it "(the tree)";
  with the tree demoted, the chess-piece set-down IS a plant-and-pat: he plants the
  based miniature on its X and pats the base once. Same verb, same puppet-lane recipe;
  if the adjudicator wants a literal tree, V4's staging swaps the miniature's pat for a
  sapling pat at zero structural cost — but the NPC pat is the better product rhyme.
- **R3 — The 90° top-down during t62–64.5 is legal** under §6's "straight-down exists
  only at the board": the camera crosses 75° elevation only after the flatten completes
  (t62), so straight-down only ever frames the finished map — which is the board's
  content by construction (G4). It never frames a standing world.
- **R4 — The throw (t62.5+) is registered as an establishing wide** in the
  `figure.check` beat table: the acting subject is `die2` (hero tier), and the goblin
  below the rising camera is deliberately under the figure floor — the handover means
  the camera leaves him. His last floor-compliant acting beat is the straighten
  (B7.2). See PHONE PASS.
- **R5 — S6→S7 is the page turn**, not a match-dissolve. The experience doc's §6 prose
  ("match-dissolve") conflicts with its own §7 seven-transition catalog, which the
  direction fixed with no eighth transition. The "hands off to dawn" reads as a
  scrub-tied `sky()` warm inside V5's tilt-up (sky tweens are not transitions), then a
  paper-flash cut at t57.5. This is also what `timeline.ts:876–887` already ships.

All hard cuts below at t50–57.5 keep the shipped times (`timeline.ts:740–744`:
50 + i·1.25) and the shipped montage disc positions x = 0, 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, z = −40
(`world.ts:3396`, pinned by direction §7's seam argument). Nothing in this chapter
re-times anything.

## STAGE 6 — THE MANY JOBS (t50–57.5, 8% of scroll, C5, silent)

State: Performance throughout — **no freeze, no frontier, no markAlive in this stage**
(direction §7: "No frontier in … S6"). Air: `skyVellum #EEE6D2`, bright, flat,
weightless. One soft day-family key (+18° azimuth, `rigs.ts` preset) per vignette,
never changing mid-vignette. Every cut is the page turn: one frame of paper, never
black, reversible. The chapter numeral reads `C5`; the 66-tick ruler visibly
accelerates — the interface itself says "montage tempo". No rest anchors inside the
stage (locked: the one stage that rewards momentum).

The six discs become **six square work-sheet islets**: small square cards (~5×5 world
units) with the full island grammar at worksheet scale — sectioned three-band cut
edge, a drawn rim contour that stops being drawn, grid ghost at ≤`GRID_INK` running a
few cells onto the paper, and **non-verbal draughting marks in the margins** (dimension
ticks, one arrow, an X where a prop will stand — `pencil.ts` primitives, never a font).
The v1 cylinders + rim + hatch ring (`world.ts:3398–3416`, hatch at 3409) are deleted.
Each islet reads as a page from the keeper's workbook; the montage is him working
through the stack.

The S3 grammar reprised at tempo: in each vignette, the one touched thing banks its
life — one idle begins as his hand leaves it, on the world clock, and keeps running
until the next page turn.

---

### B6.0 — THE ROAD (t50–51.25)

1. **BEAT + ARGUMENT.** t50 page-turn in off `welcome` (cleared by t49.0). Argument:
   *the heroic night is over; this is the job, and the job includes drawing the world
   itself.* First belief: the goblin authors maps.
2. **MESSAGE.** none (montage stays silent — locked decision). Meaning is carried by
   the cut grammar: paper flash → a workbook page → one job done in one gesture. The
   accelerating ruler carries "tempo".
3. **VISUAL.** Vignette camera solve inherited from `timeline.ts:721–738` shot 0:
   lens ≤3 units out, just outboard of his stand, shooting down the line from him to
   the job, above the work surface; 0.09 push-in drift over the cut (`:785`). Islet 0:
   the map table (timber class, ruled silhouette kept, `bakeBark` grain) carrying the
   map sheet — paper-props class: `dieBone` ground, authored illegible scribble-rows
   one direction, dog-eared corner, held by two painted weight stones; quill + inkpot
   beside. Foreground: the islet's near cut edge in section (plane one). Subject plane:
   the sheet and his hand. The **fence-post carpenter's pencil** (hero tier #5, scaled
   up) leans against the table. Far: bare paper void — the islet edge in frame (sheet
   edge rule). Painted: everything on the islet. Graphite: the road's construction —
   dimension ticks and one arrow in the sheet's margin marking where the road must
   reach.
4. **3D ELEMENTS.** Islet card 0 (NEW, islandKit at worksheet scale) · map table
   (reuse carpentry: table) · map sheet + quill + inkpot (reuse keeping-props register)
   · fence-post pencil (reuse hero #5, rescaled) · **brush + pigment pot (reuse hero
   #6 — its one on-camera use in the film)** · 2 weight stones (rock kit, merged) ·
   draughting-mark set (NEW, shared across all six islets). The road mark itself is a
   per-mesh-material prop (it animates: the v1 `roadLine` scale-from-anchor mechanism,
   `world.ts:3468–3478`, kept — resurfaced as an inked road stroke, not an `ember` box).
   Table + stones + pot merge into the islet's static geometry; sheet, road, pencil,
   brush stay separate (animated/held).
5. **GOBLIN ACTION.** He is already mid-arrival on the cut (shipped grammar: gait in,
   last stride along his own facing, `timeline.ts:799–807`). A draughtsman's `stoop`
   over the sheet; the pencil sweeps and the road draws itself under the sweep
   (scrub-tied, `roadLine.scale.x → 1` as today). Then — the trilayer's origin story
   as two props — he swaps pencil for brush: **one `touchUp` stroke** (used exactly
   once in the film, here) and the road's paint side arrives along the bristle line.
   He does not exit; the page turns on him.
6. **INTERACTION.** None — scroll only. Responsiveness: the road ink is 1:1 with the
   scrub; drag backwards and the road un-draws, the brush stroke un-paints. That
   reversal IS the feedback.
7. **ANIMATION.** Master timeline: the cut, the push-in drift, the stoop, the pencil
   sweep, the road scale, the touchUp stroke. World clock (banked on hand-leave): the
   sheet's held corner settles with a paper flutter ≤2px, once, then still. Reverses
   cleanly: all scrub-tied tweens. Special reverse care: the vignette-entry `tl.set`s
   (position/rotation/speed) must stay paired at the cut position so reverse replays
   them in reverse order (motion doc §4 note) — this binds all six vignettes.
8. **TRANSITION OUT.** The page turn at t51.25 (1-frame paper flash). Cost: nothing
   created or destroyed — both islets are resident (`montageSet` visible 49.5–57.7,
   `timeline.ts:161`); a camera `cut()` + goblin relocate `tl.set`s.
9. **KEEPING.** The pencil is worn short and the pot lid sits crooked — handled tools.
   The sheet's margin ticks say the road was measured before it was drawn. Second
   plane, whisper only. Not a flagship.

### B6.1 — THE MONSTER (t51.25–52.5)

1. **BEAT + ARGUMENT.** Argument: *he stocks the encounters too.* The player reads
   "monster"; the DM reads "encounter placement."
2. **MESSAGE.** none. The X on the ground carries it: the monster lands where the mark
   said it would.
3. **VISUAL.** Shot 1 solve kept (far-side stand, `timeline.ts:728`, standoff floor
   for the haunch, `:769–773`). Islet 1: bare worksheet with a single graphite **X**
   at centre (draughting mark) and a scuffed ring where the X has been redrawn —
   value-step wear, not an eraser ghost. The monster rears to ~1.6u; the goblin works
   it from the far side so both read. Light: the soft key gives the bulk one committed
   shadow side. Painted: monster, goblin, islet. Graphite: the X, margin ticks.
4. **3D ELEMENTS.** Islet card 1 (NEW) · **the monster** — geometry kept verbatim
   (`world.ts:3487–3660`: lathe bulk, bent arms, brow bar, lantern eyes, underbite +
   tusks), surface repainted: `monsterHide` gouache in 3 quantized tiers on the bulk,
   and the **tick-stroke shag kept as authored language** (`world.ts:3532–3563` — the
   direction names it "already correct, authored specifically as not-hatch"); claws
   `caveDark`, tusks `gobTooth`, eyes `flameCore` (kept — the fixed under-read). One
   per-mesh material root for the scale-in transform is NOT needed (transforms don't
   need material state); the monster group merges internally where static.
5. **GOBLIN ACTION.** Two-handed set-down (shipped case 1 staging, `timeline.ts:822–829`):
   `crouch`, both-hands `reach`, `express('strain')` — the monster grows from zero
   under his hands (`PUPPET.pop`), lands ON the X — step back, `armRest` both sides,
   `express('smug')`.
6. **INTERACTION.** None. Reverse-scrub shrinks the monster back into his hands —
   legible, funny, free.
7. **ANIMATION.** Master: cut, drift, set-down, monster scale. World clock (banked):
   the monster takes ONE idle breath cycle (chest scale ±1%) after his hands leave —
   the encounter is now alive. Freeze-safe by construction (no freeze here). Reverses
   cleanly; the breath is world-clock so it never runs backwards, it just stops being
   banked before the touch (visibility of idle gated on the scrub-tied "set-down done"
   flag, same as S3 props).
8. **TRANSITION OUT.** Page turn at t52.5. Cost: camera cut + relocate sets.
9. **KEEPING.** The redrawn X's scuffed ring — this encounter slot has been used
   before. Second plane. Not a flagship.

### B6.2 — THE SIGN (t52.5–53.75)

1. **BEAT + ARGUMENT.** Argument: *the world's dressing — signage, the reads players

2. **MESSAGE.** none. The tankard device on the sign carries "tavern" alone.
3. **VISUAL.** Shot 2 solve kept (drop above his reach, lens low and back,

4. **3D ELEMENTS.** Islet card 2 (NEW) · wall fragment + planks + plinth (reuse,
   re-surfaced; hatch at `world.ts:3687` deleted) · bracket + brace + scroll curl
   (reuse) · **tavern sign + chains** (reuse register: sign face gets the paper-props
   scribble-row treatment for its border, painted tankard device kept,
   `world.ts:3723–3762`). Sign is transform-animated (drop) — no per-mesh material
   needed. Wall merges static.
5. **GOBLIN ACTION.** **`hang`** (new verb, puppet lane): he guides the drop in from
   under it — `reach` up, `express('strain')` — the sign falls onto the bracket
   (`PUPPET.drop`, the film's one sanctioned bounce, motion doc adjudication 2), then
   `tap`s it level twice.
6. **INTERACTION.** None. The drop's bounce is the frame's own responsiveness.
7. **ANIMATION.** Master: cut, drift, hang, drop, taps. World clock (banked): the sign
   swings on its chains in a decaying pendulum (~3 swings, then still) after the tap.

8. **TRANSITION OUT.** Page turn at t53.75.
9. **KEEPING.** The bracket's underside is rubbed bright where chains have swung for
   years (metal class: rubbed-bright on gripped/worn parts) — this is not the first
   sign it has held. Second plane. Not a flagship.

### B6.3 — THE CHEST (t53.75–55)

1. **BEAT + ARGUMENT.** Argument: *treasure is placed, and JUDGED — the loot the party
   finds was decided by someone who cared.* The comic beat of the montage.
2. **MESSAGE.** none. The judging gesture carries it: one coin held up to the light,
   turned, approved, dropped. One rejected coin already sits beside the chest.
3. **VISUAL.** Shot 4 solve kept, moved to disc 3 (lens drops to meet the low subject,
   `timeline.ts:734–735`). Islet 3: the chest (timber class: box construction,
   end-arcs, strap lines on the Prep side, corner-lightening on the handled lid edge)
   open, hoard inside as painted coin mass (`gold` gouache, one authored glint stroke
   on the topmost coin — miniature-painter dot-and-line, no specular). The v1
   `hoardTone` hatch (`world.ts:3809`) is deleted; ground tone is baked islet albedo.
   Two crates behind (merged).
4. **3D ELEMENTS.** Islet card 3 (NEW) · chest + judged coins (reuse register:
   `buildChest` re-surfaced) · 2 crates (reuse, merged static) · 3 loose singleton
   coins: two in-flight props (animated, per-transform), one rejected coin lying
   beside the chest (static, merged). Chest lid transform-animated.
5. **GOBLIN ACTION.** Crouched at the open chest: **`coinDrop`** (new verb) — lift a
   coin, hold it up (beat), drop it in; a second coinDrop at a faster clip; the third
   coin gets the longer look and a head-tilt, then drops. Three drops inside one 1.25t
   window, the last one landing as the page turns — diligence at tempo.
6. **INTERACTION.** None. Reverse: coins un-drop into his hand — the judging replays
   backwards intact.
7. **ANIMATION.** Master: cut, drift, crouch, three coinDrops, lid already open on the
   cut (the lid-opening was v1's beat; v2's beat is the judging — the lid opens in the

   glint is baked. What holds still: the hoard mass, always.
8. **TRANSITION OUT.** Page turn at t55.
9. **KEEPING.** The rejected coin beside the chest — a decision made visible, the
   evidence layer's whole doctrine in one prop. Second plane. Not a flagship.

### B6.4 — THE NPC (t55–56.25)

1. **BEAT + ARGUMENT.** Argument: *people are placed like pieces — and the pieces are
   tokens.* The most product-literal beat in the film: a painted figure on a visible
   base IS a token. Plants the S7/S8 payoff (figures resolve to token discs).
2. **MESSAGE.** none. The X on the village square carries it: mark → placement — the
   same grammar a DM performs on the product's map.
3. **VISUAL.** Shot 5-class tightness but staged as shot 3's side (alternation held):
   lens ~2.8 out, slightly high, down the line from him to the village square. Islet
   4: a **miniature village** — three gabled houses (carpentry register: "gabled house
   (montage + miniature)"), a lane of the islet's baked albedo, the **sapling trio**
   at the village edge (R1: trees as dressing) with a fresh pat-mark in the soil and a
   draughting X where the next tree goes. At the square's centre: the placement **X**.
   He enters carrying the **NPC based miniature** — a painted figure (cloth class,
   `cloakIndigo`, silhouette-first, never out-chroma-ing him) on a visible `dieBone`
   base disc, one cell across.
4. **3D ELEMENTS.** Islet card 4 (NEW) · **NPC based miniature (NEW — the register's
   one new cast prop; hero-adjacent polish at its scale)** · gabled house ×3 (reuse,
   merged per class) · sapling trio (reuse flora kit, merged) · draughting marks
   (shared set). The miniature is transform-animated (carried, set down) — held mesh,
   no material state needed.
5. **GOBLIN ACTION.** He walks in with the miniature held ahead of him like a chess
   piece, two deliberate steps — the script's own simile made literal — then
   **`plantAndPat`** (R2): plants the base exactly on the X, pats it once, and leans
   back to check the sightline to the tavern-ward house, the way a DM squares a token
   to the grid.
6. **INTERACTION.** None. The base-on-X registration is the frame's answer: precision
   as feedback.
7. **ANIMATION.** Master: cut, drift, carry-walk, plantAndPat, the lean-back. World
   clock: **nothing banks — the miniature never idles.** It is a piece, not a
   creature; its stillness among five idling vignettes is the product rhyme, on
   purpose. Reverses cleanly (pure transforms).
8. **TRANSITION OUT.** Page turn at t56.25.
9. **KEEPING.** The sapling trio's pat-marked soil (the folded tree job, kept as
   evidence someone plants here) and the X's placement — habitual tense, exactly as
   §2 assigns S6. Second plane. Not a flagship.

9. **KEEPING.** The wax runs down one side of every candle — **these candles have
   burned many nights before tonight.** The book's dog-eared corner. Second plane.
   Not a flagship.

### B6.6 — THE TILT TO DAWN (t57.1–57.5)

1. **BEAT + ARGUMENT.** Argument: *the montage was one night of many, and the night is
   ending.* Sets the verdict stage's air before a word is spent.
2. **MESSAGE.** none. The sky itself is the message: vellum warms toward dawn.
3. **VISUAL.** The camera tilts up from the three flames along the table line, past
   the islet's rim (sheet-edge rule honoured at the top of the move), to the paper
   void warming: `sky()` tween `skyVellum → skyDawn` direction, scrub-tied, landing
   just short so the t57.5 `skyCut` to `skyDawn` (`timeline.ts:887`) is invisible.
   The flames' glow holds the frame bottom; the cliff is NOT visible (it lives at
   x≈120; the montage faces z — the "cliff in the distance" prose from the experience
   doc is dropped as geometrically false; the dawn sky does the handoff alone).
4. **3D ELEMENTS.** None new. `cliffSet` becomes visible at t57.0 behind the cut
   (`timeline.ts:166`) — free, off-camera.
5. **GOBLIN ACTION.** He stays at the table below frame, done. No acting beat.
6. **INTERACTION.** None. The tilt is scrub-tied; dragging back re-descends to the
   flames.
7. **ANIMATION.** Master: the tilt (camera `cam()` move, settle lane), the sky warm.
   World clock: flame flicker continues under the tilt — the last live thing in frame.
8. **TRANSITION OUT.** **The page turn** at t57.5 (R5) — the montage's last paper
   flash, into the cliff. Cost: camera cut, goblin relocate set (`timeline.ts:877`),
   `remains` hidden / `tended` shown sets (`:880–881`), `skyCut`. `montageSet` goes
   invisible at 57.7 (`:161`).
9. **KEEPING.** Carried by B6.5's wax. Not a flagship.

## STAGE 7 — THE HANDOVER (t57.5–64.5, 12% of scroll, C6)

State: Performance → the flatten (the film's second and last seam frontier). Air:
`skyDawn #E6C1A2`; low dawn key, exterior-day family (+18° — the cliff's one bake
serves S1 night and S7 day precisely because the azimuth held). Painted god-ray cones
in `rayGold` — light as a painted object, never a flare. Rest anchors: the
tended-cairn read, and between the pitch lines. The two most product-forward captions
in the film sit on its most spectacular minute — spectacle serving the sentence.

The cliff island is the S1/S2 asset in its second era of dressing. The miniature world
below is v1's `miniWorld` topology (`world.ts:4125–4313`) kept and re-surfaced — a
real miniature, not a desk. All hatch dies: cracks (3952) → painted value-break
fractures in the rock bake; scorches (4016/4027/4044) → gone with the remains;
massif tone (4208) → reserved-paper snow + 3-tier rock; water (4260) → water-class
pigment band with tangent-aligned lit dabs (the S7 river is the class's one funded
pigment use); till (4297) → painted field washes.

### B7.1 — THE TENDED RIM (t57.5–58.0) — FLAGSHIP BEAT 4

1. **BEAT + ARGUMENT.** Page-turn lands on the S1 rim angle — the angle-echo bookend
   (`cut(57.5, [119.5,6.3,1.8] → [122.6,6.3,0])`). Argument: *the ruin from the
   film's first minute has been kept.* The visitor believed the goblin works; now they
   believe he has been working HERE, on the wound they watched happen, since before
   they arrived. This is the receipt `pitch1` cashes.
2. **MESSAGE.** none — the visual rhyme does it in half a second (locked). What
   carries meaning: same camera, same rock, opposite evidence — remains gone, cairn
   raised, mushrooms planted.
3. **VISUAL.** Half a beat on the S1/S3 cliff-top angle, elevation inside the bench
   clamp. Foreground: the rim lip with the **cairn** (five slab stones, cool stone,
   flat-stacked — shipped geometry `world.ts:4061–4080`) and the **three mushrooms**
   (caps in threes, never symmetric, `:4082–4092`). Middle: the goblin at his rim
   stance. Far: dawn paper beyond the rim (sheet edge in frame). The one authored
   framing this flagship gets (composition rule: flagships are framed inside their own
   moment — here the moment is the cut itself; no freeze exists in S7, and none is
   added). Light: dawn key low; one god-ray cone grazes the rim from frame right,
   painted.
4. **3D ELEMENTS.** Cliff island (reuse — S1/S2 asset, day bake) · tended dressing
   (KEPT — already built, hidden→shown at 57.5) · remains hidden (shipped sets) ·
   god-ray cone ×1 (NEW, `rayGold` painted cone with drawn edge) · **the S7
   eraser-ghost decal (NEW, one of the film's exactly four):** a `graphiteLight`
   erased scorch-ring beside the cairn — the mark of the damage, rubbed out, with the
   cairn standing on it. The flagship's supporting-cast pentimento.
5. **GOBLIN ACTION.** `settle` on the cut (shipped, `timeline.ts:891`). He stands at
   the rim where the rubbed patch is, back half to us, looking down at the world. No
   task — for the first time in the film, there is nothing here left to do.
6. **INTERACTION.** Rest anchor at the tended-cairn read (touch soft-rest lands here).
   Otherwise none; the frame's responsiveness is the anchor's gentle magnetism.
7. **ANIMATION.** Master: the cut, the settle. World clock: nothing — the rim is
   still; stillness after six busy vignettes IS the beat. Reverses to the page turn
   cleanly (paired sets).
8. **TRANSITION OUT.** Plain intra-stage camera cut at t58.0 to the over-the-shoulder
   (`cut(58.0, [117.5,7.4,3.2] → [123,6.6,0])`) — shipped grammar, not a catalog
   transition (same class as S1's internal cuts). Cost: zero.
9. **KEEPING.** **This IS flagship beat 4** — the fourth of four, named by the
   direction. The cairn + mushrooms + the erased scorch-ring under them: repair,
   planting, and pentimento in one foreground.

### B7.2 — THE STRAIGHTEN + `pitch1` (t58.0–58.5)

1. **BEAT + ARGUMENT.** Argument: *"I've built worlds for your DM for years" is a
   conclusion, not a claim.* The visitor has read receipts for eight stages; the line

## S8 — THE FULL ENDCARD DESIGN

### The board's authored content — why it is the film's own world

`bakeBoardMap()` (G4: hand-authored in this repo, in code, one deterministic 2048²
canvas bake, `src/film/stages/board.ts`) paints **the map of the world the visitor
just walked**, in the product's own vocabulary — because the film's last frame is the
product's first frame, and because the flatten's destination art is UV slices of this
same atlas (they cannot drift). Content, oriented to the S7 top-down:

- **The battle grid** at `GRID_INK` — the board's underdrawing IS the grid (the third
  truth: a map is already both drawing and paint).
- **The village** (the S6 gabled-house icons) with **one NPC token disc** at one-cell
  diameter on the square where he planted the miniature — `cloakIndigo` ring on
  `dieBone`.
- **Three party token discs** at the road-head nearest the cliff mark — `cloakIndigo`
  ×2, `cloakCrimson` ×1: the S1 trio, arrived, mid-session. **One monster token** near
  a cave-mouth mark (`monsterHide` ring): the S6 encounter, placed. Tokens are what a
  DM recognizes in half a second: *this map is being played.*
- **Inked roads at 2px** (roadA/roadB's meanders), **the river as bare paper with a
  drawn edge** plus its pigment band, **six field washes**, **illustrated canopy
  blobs** at the tree stands, **the massif in ink** with reserved-paper snow, **two
  painted flame marks** on the ember-roof houses, and **the cliff as a crag-mark with
  a cairn dot** — the flagship's location, findable by anyone who scrubs back.
- **Edge-handling wear** at the margins (drybrush lightening, a rubbed corner). **No
  pentimenti**, no goblin-green anywhere, no `#B6D648` anywhere on the board.
- Double rule + corner trim marks kept from v1's trim grammar (`world.ts:4357–4384`),
  now painted into the bake.

At rest the board does not pan, zoom, or accept pointer events; it breathes ≤0.5%.

### The CTA — the film's one taught rule, performed by the visitor

Grammar: eleven scenes taught *what the goblin touches comes alive*. The button is
drawn; the visitor's pointer is the touch.

| State | Spec |
|---|---|
| **Rest (drawn)** | Graphite outline, paper fill, label **"Join the Discord"** in Cinzel 700 letterspaced caps (`JOIN THE DISCORD`), ≥44px hit area. Second border offset 2–3px, rotated 0.4°, lower opacity, boiling ≤0.8px — a drawn-world object with a hand-redrawn line. Self-evidently a button even at rest. |
| **Hover / focus-visible (touch-lit)** | Amber `#F2C35E` blooms through the letterforms **from the pointer-entry side**, 180ms; contact shadow arrives beneath **alongside the colour** (the film's rule: shadows arrive with paint); offset border re-inks to 0.9°; fill inverts to ink / paper text per copy-spec. Focus-visible gets the **identical bloom** (keyboard visitors get the grammar too) **plus** the drawn double-line focus rectangle — the offset-border language, never the browser default, never suppressed. |
| **Active (press)** | Fill deepens to ink, label to paper, 2px settle — the one physical press on the site. |
| **Click** | Opens `DISCORD_URL` in a new tab, `rel="noopener"`. **The send-off:** the die beside the wordmark rolls once to 20. Focus and site state intact on tab-return. |
| **Unset URL** | The button does not render; the subline stands alone. A dead `#` never ships (`DISCORD_URL`, single wired constant in `App.tsx`, owner: Nayan). |

### The conversion argument the whole frame makes

Read top to bottom, the frame is a complete syllogism: the wordmark names who kept the
world (the character you now like); the board proves what the keeping produces (a real
playable map of a story you just verified, tokens mid-session); the tagline names the
category in four words ("The Dungeon Master's backstage."); the subline names the two
product halves and the promise ("Build the maps. Run the table. The goblin does the
rest."); and one warm button is the only touchable thing on the page — lit by the
same amber every fire in the film was lit with. No feature list, no second CTA, no
footer, nothing below. A DM who arrived cold at t64.5 via the skip note gets the
identical frame and still understands: map builder + live table, one goblin, one door.

## PHONE PASS (390×844; floor ≥84px portrait per acting beat, `figure.check`)

- **S6:** every vignette lens already sits ≤3 units out and shoots down the
  goblin-to-job line precisely because a phone frame is 36° wide (the shipped solve's
  own comment, `timeline.ts:711–715`) — the figure floor is met by camera distance
  (mechanism tier 1) in all six. Each vignette additionally carries a `portraitLook`
  (tier 2): a tighter re-composition of the same moment — V0 favours sheet + hand, V2
  crops the wall to bracket + drop, V4 frames miniature + X + near house and lets the
  other houses go off-frame. Islets never crop on all four sides (each shows a rim);
  no restack needed — one islet per shot by construction.
- **S7:** B7.1/B7.2 are acting beats and pass by distance + a `portraitLook` that
  tightens the OTS (rim + him + the world's near half; the massif may exit frame —
  the wide establishing read happens in B7.3's rise instead, which is the "drop the
  wide" tier working as designed). B7.3–B7.5: not acting beats (establishing —
  exempt). B7.6 the throw: **registered establishing (R4)** — die2 is the actor; his
  release is authored as a large silhouette gesture. The die's painted numerals and
  the B7.7 20-face are QA'd at 390px exactly (clarity contract §11.5).
- **S8:** no goblin. Endcard clamps are copy-spec law: stack 88vw under 500px,
  wordmark 76vw, subline caps to two balanced lines, caption/halo contrast ≥4.5:1
  verified at 390×844. Board wear marks demote to texture at 390 if they cannot read
  (the direction's own demotion rule).

## ACCESSIBILITY PASS

- **Reduced motion (stepped picture book, motion §14; `A = 0` = still at the lit
  pose):** S6 — the page turns become plain cuts (no flash frame); each vignette holds
  one composition with the job in its **finished** state (road drawn, monster placed,
  sign hung, coins in, NPC on its X, candles lit); banked idles are stilled at the lit
  pose. S7 — the rise becomes three held compositions (rim / miniature / top-down);
  the flatten becomes a single cross-fade between the standing and flat states (the
  same `uTriFlat` + scale endpoints, opacity-stepped, no sweep); DOF breath dropped;
  the throw becomes a cut to the 20 face. S8 — wipes become fades at the same
  times/durations, CTA scale drops (both shipped); board breath off (static); boil
  static. Live `matchMedia`, no reload.
- **Screen reader:** the canvas is `aria-hidden`. The SR document (first in DOM)
  carries, verbatim and in order: a one-sentence montage scene description (the twelve
  captions themselves are silent through S6), `pitch1`, `pitch2`, then the endcard
  copy — tagline, subline — and the real Discord link as a real `<a>`. The CTA is a
  real link in the visual layer too (live DOM, Cinzel); focus order SR-skip → replay →
  CTA; focus ring always visible, drawn.
- **Keyboard:** ↓/↑ rest anchors (S7's two anchors; S6 has none by design — PgDn
  jumps the chapter), `End` lands the endcard, Esc de-escalates play mode; play mode
  ending moves focus to the CTA with `preventScroll`.
- **Vestibular:** the rise is slow, straight, axis-locked; no roll anywhere in the
  chapter; cuts are instant; the flatten sweeps in-world (texture/scale change, not
  camera motion).
- **Color independence:** the flatten is never colour-only — geometry lies down,
  strokes change class, the grid rises; the CTA's states pair colour with border
  re-ink + shadow + fill inversion.

## RISKS

1. **`bakeBoardMap()` is the chapter's whole bet.** A code-authored 2048² map that
   must read as *real product art* under guardrail 4 ("smooth masses and gradient
   washes rejected on sight") — and it is the conversion surface AND the flatten's
   destination atlas. Budget it like the hero: it will eat iterations. Mitigation:
   its vocabulary is fixed (G4 list) and it is judged flat at `NoToneMapping`.
2. **Endcard contrast on a busy board.** The shipped `BOARD_WASH 0.5` + per-glyph
   halos were tuned against an empty grid; a fully painted map underneath is a harder
   knockout test. QA the halo system against the final bake at 390px and 1920px
   before calling S8 done; the wash value may need to rise (it may not fall — the
   printed-content read depends on it).
3. **~32 per-mesh flatten materials** against the film-wide ≤40 budget leaves ~8 for
   every other stage's `markAlive`/`reveal` needs combined. If Chapter One/Two
   overdraw, the mountain's shoulders and the field group are the first candidates to
   share a material via merged flatten groups (fields already share one atlas region
   each; merging the six into two lie-down groups saves 4 slots at the cost of
   coarser stagger).
4. **The flatten reverse at flick speed** is the site's most-scrubbed moment. G7's
   same-mesh construction makes it correct by design, but the x-keyed stagger + seamX
   must be driven from one timeline position (no callbacks — they don't reverse;
   motion §4). Build it as pure tweens, walk it both directions at flick speed on the
   QA grid.
5. **Seven-into-six (R1/R2).** My resolution demotes tree-planting to dressing and
   stages `plantAndPat` on the NPC base. If the adjudicator overrules, the swap is
   contained to B6.4's staging text — no timing, camera, or asset change beyond
   putting a sapling in his hands instead of the miniature (and losing the token
   rhyme, which I'd argue against).
6. **Monster repaint under the no-hatch gate.** The tick-shag is pre-cleared by the
   direction, but the 3-tier bulk bake must not read as banded stripes at vignette
   distance — the quantizer's tiers ride `roughen()` displacement, not parallel bands;
   check at the vignette lens, not in isolation.
7. **God-ray cones** are one gradient-wash accident away from violating guardrail 4.
   They must be painted objects: drawn edge lines, dab-textured fill, hard stop —
   never a soft alpha falloff.
8. **The throw's figure-floor classification (R4)** is an authored exemption; if
   `figure.check` is written strictly ("every beat where he moves"), it will fail the
   throw at 390px. The check's beat table must carry the acting/establishing flag per
   beat — this chapter's table is the source of truth for S6–S8 rows.
9. **Page-turn reversibility at speed:** six paired `tl.set` clusters (position,
   rotation, speed, redress visibility at 57.5) replay in reverse order only if they
   stay paired at identical positions — a drifted set is an invisible bug until
   someone scrubs backwards through the montage. Assert in `motion.check`.
